entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:1
segments: Not enter into the congregation of the Lord; not be admitted to worship in the temple.  This was designed to prevent Israelitish parents from mutilating their children, as was often done among the heathen.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:2
segments: Every thing should be avoided by parents which tends to deprive children of any of the privileges and blessings of the people of God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:3
segments:
Ammonite--Moabite; these nations bordered upon that part of Canaan which lay east of the Jordan. 
 
Sins committed by parents may, long after they are dead, entail great evils on their children--and sins committed by rulers, great evils on the people.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:7
segments: Brother; relative, being descended like themselves from Abraham and Isaac.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:8
segments: Shall enter into the congregation; become entitled to all the privileges of an Israelite, if they embrace his religion.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:9
segments:
The host; the army of Israel. 
 
vv 9-14 
 
The individuals of an army, even when going forth to battle, are all, from the commander-in-chief to the lowest subaltern, sacredly bound to be holy in body and spirit; to indulge no feelings and allow no actions which shall not be pleasing to God, and tend to fit them for the purity, the employments, and the bliss of heaven.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:10
segments:
vv 10-14. 
 
  Wash himself; these regulations were designed to promote cleanliness and a conviction of the necessity of internal as well as external purity.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:16
segments: The oppression of servants, depriving them of their rights, or in any way injuring them, is forbidden by Jehovah.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:18
segments:
The hire; the wages of iniquity must not be offered to the Lord, as was done by the heathen. 
 
  A dog; a male prostitute, a sodomite. 
 
The gains and the practices of iniquity are an abomination to the Lord; and no offerings are acceptable to him but those of honest, upright, believing, and affectionate hearts.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:19
segments: Usury; interest.  This was designed to inculcate and increase the habit of assisting and doing good to one another as the people of God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:20
segments: Proper compensation for the use of money or any other property is not in itself wrong; but we should kindly assist the poor, and as we have opportunity and ability do good to all, especially to the friends of God and those who will use our kindness in honoring him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:23
segments: What we promise, if it is not wicked or impracticable, we should be very careful to do: it is better not to promise, than to promise and not perform.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 23:24
segments:
Eat grapes thy fill; enough to satisfy present want. 
 
  Not put any in thy vessel; to carry it away.
